items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like WindowFrameBoundary and buildWindowSpecContent say what they do, but the dialect code uses single-letter names in business logic (`for (const [i, w] of windows.entries())`, `w.spec`, `w.name`) and builds separators by hand instead of calling sql.join(chunks, sql`, `).

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The spec builder is shared, but name validation in .window() is copied five times (once per dialect) instead of using one assert helper. The manual separator loop for the WINDOW clause is also repeated in all five dialects. The file is in sql/expressions rather than sql/functions, against the stated convention.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: preceding/following check typeof, Number.isInteger and non-negativity, and their errors name the helper. .window() rejects empty and whitespace-only names. A rank getter supports the from/to order check. sql.raw only receives validated integers. All hidden tests pass.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: Purely additive: optional `windows?:` field on all five *SelectConfig types, an identical .window() on pg/mysql/sqlite/gel/singlestore, and an undefined windowSql leaves existing SQL unchanged. However, the exports come from sql/expressions/index.ts instead of sql/functions as the convention asks.
